description:
First release. Four patches for RailOne (org.cris.aikyam):

- **Disable native security SDK** - stops `AikyamApplication.onCreate()` loading `libnative-lib.so` (root cause of the app force-stopping and wiping its own data on a re-signed build).
- **Bypass USB-debugging detection** - `adb_enabled`, `adb_wifi_enabled`, `development_settings_enabled` -> false.
- **Bypass signature verification** - the app's own SHA-256 certificate check -> true.
- **Bypass rjsniffer ADB check** - the `armys/rjsniffer` isolated-process check.

Verified on a Motorola Edge 50 Neo against RailOne 2.1.66: Morphe CLI applied all four patches to the real split bundle, the merged APK installed as an in-place upgrade, and the app stayed alive with USB debugging enabled (no anti-tamper wipe, no native-library failure).

Supply the app yourself; the bundle pins the genuine Play signing certificate and rejects a modified original.

Not affiliated with or authored by the Morphe project.

patches.name: Bypass rjsniffer ADB check
patches.description: Neutralises the rjsniffer library's own adb_enabled check. It runs in the app's isolated :com.emrys.rjsniffer.rjsniffer.Sniffer process, independently of the main app.

patches.name: Bypass signature verification
patches.description: Forces the app's own signing-certificate check (SHA-256 of the APK signature) to return true, so a re-signed build is accepted by the Flutter layer.

patches.name: Bypass USB-debugging detection
patches.description: Forces the adb_enabled, adb_wifi_enabled and development_settings_enabled checks to return false, so the app runs normally while USB debugging / developer options are on.

patches.name: Disable native security SDK
patches.description: Stops AikyamApplication.onCreate() from loading libnative-lib.so, disarming the native anti-tamper SDK that force-stops the app and wipes its data. Root cause fix: the other patches only matter once this one is applied.
